# EveryO

> A Python neural computing framework built from scratch on NumPy for learning,
> teaching, and small-scale experiments. The code implements tensors, reverse-mode
> differentiation, layers, optimizers, training, and serialization.

## Scope and limits

The documented CPU workflow supports Python 3.9–3.12. The core dependencies are
NumPy and Matplotlib. Version 0.2.0 is declared in the reviewed pyproject.toml.
MIT licensed. Local core workflows require no account, API key, or telemetry.
Installation may download packages. Optional components include TensorFlow
reference checks, CUDA kernels, and ONNX export.

EveryO is not a production training runtime. GPU runtime tests require hardware
not available in the project's CI; CPU stand-ins validate transfer counting for
the separate resident-buffer API. Multi-node collectives have been exercised
across processes over TCP, not across separate physical machines. The traced
ONNX exporter specializes the graph to the traced control flow. Validate exported
models with the target runtime. Dynamic int8 quantization changes size and
fidelity rather than providing a faster NumPy kernel.

The reported 99.3% accuracy on 600 held-out digits is an example-run measurement,
not a benchmark or performance guarantee. Test counts depend on installed extras
and hardware; use current CI rather than quoting a fixed total.
